newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Experts prepare ground for Albanian security force.
newsitem.headline: Experts prepare ground for Albanian security force.

text.p: An advance team of military experts from six countries on Thursday wound up its preparations for the arrival of a multinational security force which will secure key harbours and the main airport in anarchic Albania.

"The military experts from the countries sending troops have visited the main areas where the multinational troops will be installed," said Pandeli Ristani, spokesman for the Albanian Defence Ministry. "They will leave today."
The spokesman said that the 24 experts, along with one Albanian military official, would meet later on Thursday in Rome for a briefing on their findings.
"The Albanian army representative will learn there what we have do to support the multinational operation in our country," Ristani told Reuters.
The 6,000-strong U.N.-backed security force is due to begin arriving in Albania on Monday.

The troops from Italy, France, Spain, Turkey, Greece and Romania will protect the delivery of emergency food and medical supplies to Albania, which has been racked by lawlessness and violence following the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes.
More than 200 people have been killed and about 700 injured since the uprising began earlier this year.

Albania, Europe's poorest country, plunged into near-chaos when get-rich-quick pyramid investment schemes failed and armed rebels took control of the south during an unchecked spasm of looting and banditry.
Army arsenals were looted after soldiers and police abandoned their posts while thousands of automatic rifles and weapons were seized by citizens who brandished them on the streets.
A strictly enforced 8 p.m. to 7 a.m. curfew has restored a semblance of order to the capital and surrounding area, but many regions are still viewed as lawless.
The mayor of the northern town of Shkoder said that unknown assailants had fired automatic rifles at the police station on Thursday in what he described as a brief drive-by shooting.

But other reports said an armed gang exchanged gunfire with police for about 10 minutes and one officer was injured. The Shkoder police chief was replaced this week after armed bandits there attacked a car carrying Prime Minister Bashkim Fino.

In Tirana, special units of Albanian police have launched operations against gangs in recent days. Witnesses on Thursday said about 10 heavily armed and masked officers swooped down on two young men believed to be part of a group that has been firing Kalashnikov rifles into the air at night.
The police began the dawn raid by firing into the air in a show of force before grabbing the young men and beating them in full view of nearby residents. The two were then taken away in vans.
Local residents also report that special police troops have stepped up controls inside bars and restaurants in Tirana.

Italy, which will lead the multinational force and contribute 2,500 troops, first had to survive an embarassing domestic political dispute that has threatened to topple the centre-left government of Prime Minister Romano Prodi.
Prodi won support late on Wednesday to send Italian troops to Albania but at the cost of a rift with his hard left allies that exposesd his government to a confidence test in parliament.

Albanian Prime Minister Fino said his emergency all-party government was looking forward to the international military support because it meant the demoralised local police and security forces could now focus on fighting organised crime.
"The presence of these forces is very important for us because, in this difficult situation, our police are reorganising," said Fino in an interview with Reuters.
"Our police will thus have the chance to better focus on fighting against organised crime," he said, adding that Albania had sent letters of thanks to Italy's upper and lower houses.
